newsitem.title: SPAIN: Question marks cloud Endesa sale prospect.
newsitem.headline: Question marks cloud Endesa sale prospect.

text.p: The future of Spain's electricity sector and its laws must become clearer before markets can take a view on the announced sale of Spain's 66 percent state stake in electrical company Endesa, analysts said on Tuesday.

The industry ministry announced on Monday the sale would take place before the end of 1997 as part of a package of privatisations but warned that a new regulatory framework for the electrical sector would have to be set up first.

"People are pretty clueless right now," said an equity analyst at Credit Lyonnais in Madrid. "We may have a rough idea of what the 1997 tariffs cut is going to look like, but beyond that it's all guesswork -- market share, how many generating companies there will be... it's all terribly unclear."
"There's a lot we have yet to find out about the sector," echoed ABN Amro's Luis Moreno.
The Spanish state's current 66 percent stake in Endesa is valued at around 1.3 trillion pesetas and analysts predict it is unlikely to go on sale all at once.

"It would be logical for Endesa to be privatised in tranches, firstly in view of the sheer size of the privatisation and secondly because for the state that would be good in respect of a gradual improvement in its accounts," said Juan Cueto, head of analysis at Ibersecurities.
The possibility that Endesa might acquire controlling stakes in two electricity distribution firms, Sevillana and Fecsa, could be another major factor, the Credit Lyonnais analyst said.

"Endesa is mainly a generating firm and it could suffer as liberalisation hits the distribution side," the Credit Lyonnais analyst said. "But if it were to take control of Fecsa and Sevillana, it would increase its distribution share".
